WASHINGTON — The largest defense trade show in the US, the Association of the United States Army conference, came to an end today in the heart of Washington, DC. Vehicle-mounted counter-drone systems were out in force across the show floor this year, along with a variety of drone-killing missiles, numerous tactical trucks and a wide array of supporting gear. Review this year’s offerings below, and don’t miss our additional photographic coverage from the first two days of the expo here and here .
We’ve also gathered all of our reporting from AUSA 2026 in one place right here .
BAE’s AMPV-30 (Armored Multi-Purpose Vehicle) is shown here on the trade show floor at the 2026 AUSA conference in Washington. (Breaking Defense)
Diehl Defense’s Cicada counter-drone munition is an electrically propelled missile that can feature a fragmentation warhead or a safety net. (Breaking Defense)
AeroVironment’s Bullfrog M240 autonomous weapon system, seen here in the bed of a utility vehicle, has a range of 1,500 meters for defense against drone groups 1 through 3, according to AV. (Breaking Defense)

This is GM Defense’s hybrid-powered Heavy Duty Tactical Truck, which is based on the Chevrolet Silverado. The truck includes a “silent” drive mode “to reduce acoustic and thermal signatures,” the firm says at its 2026 AUSA display. (Breaking Defense)
This is the Tactical Firejet from San Diego-based Kratos Defense & Security Solutions, Inc., pictured on the show floor at the 2026 AUSA expo. The Firejet is marketed as a low-cost drone that can fly at 0.8 mach speed and with a range of 500 nautical miles. (Breaking Defense)

A Polish Air Force F-16C flies alongside a U.S. Air Force KC-135 Stratotanker assigned to the 100th Air Refueling Wing, during a refueling mission as part of Ramstein Flag 26 over Finland, June 12, 2026. (U.S. Air Force photo by Senior Airman Aidan Martínez Rosiere)
WARSAW — With Poland only partway through an air defense modernization effort, the Polish Air Force has been operating at the highest readiness on a nightly basis, which is putting heavy strain on personnel and equipment, according to Maj. Gen. Ireneusz Nowak, the operational commander for the Polish Armed Forces.
Nowak said 80 percent of his service’s attention is focused on air defense, with the ground and air components of Poland’s integrated air defenses still three to four years away.
“We are actually like maybe 30 percent advanced in that process. That means basically that we are procuring, we are acquiring new weapons systems and we are simply waiting for them to be implemented,” he said during a panel discussion at the Warsaw Security Forum.
In the meantime, the Air Force has changed how it operates in order to fill the gap. Starting Oct. 1, the service stopped following Visual Identification (VID) procedures in which a pilot confirms a target’s type, markings or nationality by sight before engaging.
Instead, they are now following Positive Identification (PI) procedures. That means that the pilot no longer needs to be close enough to see what the aircraft they are tracking is, and instead can engage based on factors such as radar data, information from other systems and intelligence, including information passed on by Ukraine.
“So now we are much more flexible, much more responsive,” Nowak, who is responsible for Polish airspace, said.
During the panel discussion, Nowak acknowledged that using fighter jets to shoot down cheap drones is a bad cost ratio for Poland, but said there simply isn’t any other option at the moment. “We need to develop massive, responsive weapons systems capable to counter-react the UAVs operations,” he said.
Lt. Gen. Rolf Folland, Norway’s Military Representative to NATO, agreed that the air superiority model of recent decades is under challenge, noting “We can’t just use all of our munitions in one blast. We have to repeat it over and over again.”
Poland should have some options, but systems that the country hoped to have ready now are still underway. Nowak pointed to the integration of Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System missiles on F-16s as a near-term solution, but said there is a hitch in getting those weapons in the field.
“It hasn’t happened yet, and we are trying to process it, but we [Polish Air Force] couldn’t get the fuses, which were utilized by the US Air Force, and were certified, because of business restrictions and limitations. So we are waiting for the new type of the fuse,” he concluded.
Nowak also mentioned the possibility of using the F/A-50GF aircraft to combat drones, which Defense Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz announced earlier this month has officially commenced combat duty. Nowak described the plane as very promising as a drone hunter and a very good tool against current threats which the Russian Federation presents, but said weapon integration challenges remain.
“So I must admit that this aircraft will be ready in maybe two years, fully operational and as a very good tool against current threats. But as always, it takes time, and the time is too long and that’s the part which frustrates me a lot,” he said.

WARSAW, Poland — European governments are encouraging their defense industries to jointly develop and produce unmanned systems with Ukrainian companies, while cautioning to simultaneously new keep tanks and armored vehicles on hand for defending NATO’s eastern flank, officials said at the Warsaw Security Forum.
Dilan Yeşilgöz-Zegerius, the deputy prime minister and defense minister of the Netherlands, highlighted the Dutch defense sector’s ties with Ukraine in the field of drones.
“Our armed forces are really training, as we speak, every day with the knowledge the Ukrainians have, because … they have the most innovative Army in Europe,” Yeşilgöz-Zegerius said on Oct. 12. “And what we are doing at the same time … is investing in our own defense industry. Because it was also, of course, due to a lack of spending, not that strong anymore. And in Europe we have that issue.”
Meanwhile, while investing in drone and counter-drone systems, NATO allies bordering Russia are also procuring heavy gear for their land forces and seeking to secure a significant share of manufacturing work for their domestic defense industries.
Lithuanian Defense Minister Robertas Kaunas told Defense News at the forum that the country’s planned acquisition of six-wheel-drive armored personnel carriers from Finland’s Patria is an example of how allies can work together on major purchases for their land forces. The vehicles are to support the Baltic state’s National Division, its main combat unit.
“One of our intentions is not only to assemble, but also be involved in the R&D process,” Kaunas said. “The National Division is important because, together with our allies, including the United States, Germany, Poland, we can block our adversaries near the front line, near our borders, and then, of course, use drones, modern types of weapons to break them.”
Kaunas said that combining the two categories of military assets is crucial, as demonstrated in Ukraine.
“Ukraine adapted tanks with additional defense anti-drone capabilities and used them as a great source of protection for their soldiers, pushing Russians back near the front lines,” the Lithuanian minister said.
Dovilė Šakalienė, a Lithuanian lawmaker and the country’s former National Defence Minister, told Defense News that European allies must sign “smart contracts” that reflect the rapidly changing battlefield reality in Ukraine, as exemplified by Lithuania’s 2024 deal to buy 44 Leopard 2A8 tanks for the country’s military, which she signed while in office.
“We need to sign smart contracts which give us the delivery of the newest technology,” Šakalienė said. “In the Leopard agreement, we also included in a very clear way a condition that the newest version of anti-drone defense systems is going to be included. Not the ones which would be ready in 2024, but the ones that will be ready at the time of the assembly of these tanks. For the development of such technology, three years is eternity.”
Despite European nations’ rapid expansion of drone procurement, allies should continue to invest in heavy equipment such as tanks and armored vehicles for their land forces, Šakalienė said.
“Massive land maneuvers cannot be completed only with drones,” she added.
Meanwhile, as Poland, the forum’s host, is making efforts to increasingly shift from the role of a buyer of foreign military gear to exporter of such goods, foreign defense groups competing for major orders are investing to expand their manufacturing footholds in the country. For U.S. companies, Poland’s drive to expand its domestic production capacities comes as many industry players are already planning to boost their capabilities in the country.
“One of the things I can say about Poland is that the workforce here is exceptional. We’ve already got 1,000 employees here in Poland. And we’re looking to have much more than that,” Vince Logsdon, vice president for international business development at Boeing Defense Space and Security, told Defense News.
Building on the 2024 deal to sell 96 AH-64E Apache attack helicopters to Poland under a deal worth around $10 billion, the producer is now offering its CH-47 Chinook aircraft to the country’s armed forces, pitching it as a complementary platform to the Apaches that can support troop movements and battlefield logistics.
“The Chinook is our offering, it has proven itself throughout the world as a vertical lift, heavy lift helicopter. It has lots of operators throughout the world, and one of the things I have seen with our CH-47 offering is that most operators that acquire the Apache, they ultimately also acquire the CH-47,” Logsdon said. “It’s a perfect combination in terms of extending the battle space for the Apache.

Jaroslaw Adamowski is the Poland correspondent for Defense News.

SHIPPENSBURG, Pa. — Volvo Trucks North America unveiled the all-new VNX on Wednesday, a vocational and heavy-haul truck built for a segment where Volvo is looking to expand its market reach. Peter Voorhoeve, president of Volvo Trucks North America, put the company’s share of North American vocational sales at 2% to 3%.
The VNX shares an electrical architecture with the long-haul VNL and regional-haul VNR , the result of what Volvo said was a $3 billion investment in product development and manufacturing.
Vocational work makes up about a quarter of the North American truck market, Voorhoeve said at a preview event at Volvo Construction Equipment’s Customer Center. Long haul accounts for half and regional haul for the remaining quarter.
“We don’t really play in that vocational segment. We have like a two or three percent market share,” Voorhoeve said. “In the largest market of the world, apart from China, why would we not play in a segment that we are so rooted in the rest of the world?”
Volvo’s FMX holds about 30% of the vocational market in both Europe and Brazil, he said. In North America, Volvo has sold the VHD since 2000. Voorhoeve said its customers are loyal, but the truck has covered a limited range of applications.
Volvo built the VNX around feedback from VHD owners, its vocational business abroad and the job-site experience of Volvo Construction Equipment, which has built and sold machines in the U.S. for more than 50 years.
“Growth in vocational is a natural next step for Volvo Trucks, right as we’re seeing stable demand for trucks on construction sites, infrastructure projects and industrial builds across the country,” Voorhoeve said in a statement.
Remote steer and a terrain brake
Remote Steer gives an operator control of the VNX from outside the cab at speeds up to 5 mph, Volvo said, aimed at mixers, cranes, vac units and other work that needs precise movement.
“Basically what we’ve done is we’ve made a giant RC truck,” said John Moore, product marketing manager at Volvo Trucks North America. “If you ever try to drive a mixer and back it in real close to a building or where they’re pouring concrete, you pretty much have to have a person to guide you. Remote steer lets a mixer be backed in with one person.”
Terrain Brake holds the truck in place on steep, rocky ground the moment the driver lifts off the accelerator, stopping forward or backward lurches faster than the driver could reach the service brakes.
A direction-change feature lets drivers switch between forward and reverse without touching the brake. Moore said it targets dump truck drivers who shuttle back and forth all day.
Configurations and powertrain
The VNX comes as a 300 day cab and a 440 with a 42-inch sleeper, each available as a tractor or straight truck, plus a 640 tractor with a 62-inch midroof sleeper. Every model is offered in axle-forward and axle-back configurations, and the heat-treated steel frame rails are rated for 160,000 pounds gross vehicle weight.
The truck runs on Volvo’s D13, rated up to 540 horsepower and 1,950 pound-feet of torque and certified to EPA 2027 emissions standards in all 50 states. Moore said that rating puts the VNX within 60 horsepower of the 600-horsepower big-block engines at the top of the class.
The 2027 D13’s engine brake climbs to 630 braking horsepower, up from 500 and above the engine’s 540-horsepower output.
“Typically engines rate their engine brake the same as their horsepower. This one is different—we have extra braking,” Moore said. That matters on steep downgrades, where service brakes can overheat.
The new I-Shift transmission shifts 30% faster, he said, and comes in 13- and 14-speed versions with crawler gears.
Safety and connectivity
Standard forward pedestrian detection scans from 23 to 230 feet, joined by blind spot detection on both sides and a 360-degree camera. The cab uses one-third more ultra-high-strength steel than Volvo’s legacy vocational trucks. Volvo said standard driver-side curtain airbags make it the only OEM in North America to offer them on a vocational truck.
Every VNX ships with a factory-installed 4G telematics gateway for remote diagnostics and over-the-air programming. Volvo said it will announce the start of sales later this year.

The Gilead Sciences deal, which include $135 million in upfront and near-term payments, marks a critical platform validation for Vir Biotechnology as investors await an upcoming readout in solid tumors.
Gilead Sciences has helped bolster the appeal of Vir Biotechnology’s T cell engager technology with a new licensing deal that includes $135 million in upfront and near-term payments—including an equity stake—and could tack on an additional $1.74 billion in milestones.
The upfront payment includes $90 million split between a $65 million cash payment and a $25 million equity stake for Gilead. Another $45 million will be paid out in near-term preclinical milestones, according to Vir’s Wednesday press release .
For its investment, Gilead will gain access to three dual-masked T cell engagers (TCEs) for solid tumors developed using Vir’s PRO-XTEN masking technology. Vir will conduct discovery before handing over development of any promising assets to Gilead.

Vir’s pipeline is anchored in hepatitis delta, with the company currently testing a combo of elebsiran and tobevibart in Phase 3. The biotech also has a variety of assets for the treatment of solid tumors in Phase 1. Vir partnered with Astellas earlier this year seeking to monetize its drug discovery engine. The Astellas deal focused on a single asset called VIR-5500 for prostate cancer.
With the Gilead deal, H.C. Wainright sees Vir’s plan paying off and sending a bigger message to potential partners.
“We view this second partnership as incremental external validation of Vir’s ability to monetize its oncology platform beyond a single clinical asset,” the firm wrote on Wednesday morning. The Gilead deal includes “attractive headline economics” for Vir, the firm added, while Gilead will shoulder the development burden.
H.C. Wainright noted, however, that Wednesday’s deal does not include new clinical evidence or identify specific targets. “We therefore view the transaction as strategic and financial validation rather than a basis to increase clinical probabilities of success.”
For more clinical validation, investors will need to wait for data from the Phase 1 ECLIPSE2/3 trial of VIR-5818 in HER2-targeted solid tumors, the firm said. A readout is expected sometime before the end of the year.
The company is expected to begin seeing revenue from the hepatitis and cancer programs in the early 2030s, H.C. Wainright said.
While Vir’s shares were steady on Wednesday morning at $10.58 apiece, the stock has risen 75% year to date.

Wisconsin-based Oshkosh Defense has begun production of the first prototype of the Dutch Expeditionary Patrol Vehicle, or DXPV.
According to the company, the new vehicle, also called the “Kaaiman,” was derived from the Joint Light Tactical Vehicle , or JLTV, and adapted for the Netherlands Ministry of Defence .
At the 2026 AUSA Annual Meeting and Exposition, Pat Williams, the company’s chief program officer, described the “production” as “an important step in delivering next-generation capability to the Netherlands.”
Compared to a standard JLTV, the DXPV has been enhanced for mobility, corrosion protection, mission systems and suspension for increased off-road performance.
“Just as importantly, it demonstrates the strength of an active production base and our ability to continuously evolve proven vehicle technologies to address the changing needs of our customers and their missions,” Williams said.
Beyond the DXPV prototype, Oshkosh officials at the show are emphasizing the company’s renewed approach toward “rapidly delivering mission-ready solutions.” The company added that it has delivered more than 200,000 tactical wheeled vehicles to U.S. and allied forces.
The Oshkosh AUSA booth also featured other platforms like its Family of Medium Tactical Vehicle A2 Low-Velocity Air Drop, or FMTV A2 LVAD, and the hybrid electric JLTV, or simply eJLTV.
With that, Williams added that “production readiness matters,” referring to how quickly Oshkosh was able to develop the DXPV. The Dutch MoD signed an agreement with Oshkosh for the vehicles last summer and then placed an order valued between $25 and $30 million in January.
“Because we’re building on a mature platform from an active production line, we can move from concept to prototype much faster than traditional vehicle development,” Williams said.

Volvo is already calling the EX60 a “game changer” as its highest-range, fastest-charging EV to date. After delaying US deliveries, Volvo’s new midsize electric SUV will remain limited, at least for now.
Volvo delays EX60 deliveries in the US
Volvo’s new midsize electric SUV is impressive. As the first model built on its new SPA3 platform, the EX60 can drive further and charge faster than any all-electric Volvo so far.
After delivering the first models in Europe this summer, Volvo said it planned to ramp up production as it rolled out to new markets, including the US.
Volvo expected to sell roughly 7,000 EX60s in the US by the end of 2026, a dealer told Automotive News , but the company is on pace to deliver just a fraction of that.

The Swedish luxury brand told dealers in a memo sent in late September that it had delayed customer deliveries, which Automotive News reviewed.
“Introducing a brand-new platform and product into a running factory is always a challenge,” Volvo’s memo said, adding that “The delays are not related to vehicle quality, safety, or product performance.”
Volvo EX60 start of production event in April (Source: Volvo)
Citing a person with knowledge of the situation, the report claims Volvo is working through a “production crisis” that will leave the US with limited inventory until early 2027.
Volvo spokesperson Jacquelyn Johnson confirmed that EX60 availability will “remain limited” in the short term. However, Johnson added that Volvo expects to distribute “a significant number” of EX60s to dealers in early 2027.
The source said Volvo will focus on deliveries in Europe, where EV sales are stronger, leaving the US on the back burner.
Volvo EX60 reveal event (Source: Volvo)
Since Volvo is using new manufacturing methods, such as megacasting, cell-to-body, and more, “the ramp-up phase takes a little longer than initially planned,” Johnson said.
The issue reportedly stems from integrating the EX60’s battery pack into the body structure and manufacturing the electric motors.
Volvo began EX60 production in April at its upgraded Torslanda plant in Gothenburg, Sweden. Initial plans called for building around 2,000 EX60s a week, but the source said output will be about 10% of that.
Volvo EX60 interior (Source: Volvo)
The 2027 Volvo EX60 starts at $58,400 and offers an EPA-estimated range of up to 307 miles. With up to 320 kW, it can add up to 155 miles in just 10 minutes of charging.
Starting at $60,750, the EX60 P10 Plus offers up to 330 miles of range. It can add up to 165 miles in 10 minutes with up to 370 kW.

Volvo’s production crisis will open the door for luxury rivals like BMW and Mercedes-Benz to gain a first-mover advantage with their next-generation electric vehicles already rolling out.

source_document.body:
Edge Logistics has sued rival freight broker Freight Tec Management Group and four former employees, alleging they diverted customers through a scheme involving confidential information and kickbacks funded by inflated freight charges.
The 51-page federal complaint, filed Sept. 30 in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois, alleges that the employees secretly established competing businesses while still working for Edge Logistics and arranged to transfer customer accounts to Utah-based Freight Tec before resigning.
Edge alleges its expedited-freight division declined 66.4% within weeks of the employees’ departures in May 2026, while the rest of its business grew 8.5%. The lawsuit does not specify whether those figures measure revenue, shipment volume or another metric, nor does it identify the precise comparison period.
The lawsuit names Freight Tec Management Group Inc., former Edge employees Nicholas Daglas, John Harlan, Andre Apiquian and Alexis Hersh, and three companies allegedly established to operate as Freight Tec brokerage agents: Parlay Expedited LLC, Thorndale Logistics LLC and Freight Redefined LLC.
Todd Rowden, a partner at Taft Stettinius & Hollister LLP representing the four former employees and three related LLCs, disputed the allegations.
“My clients dispute plaintiff’s allegations, and the legal sufficiency of its claims, and have no further comment regarding the complaint,” Rowden said in an emailed statement to FreightWaves.
Freight Tec did not provide a substantive response to FreightWaves’ requests for comment before publication.
Lawsuit alleges employees planned departures while still on payroll
According to the complaint, the four employees worked in Edge’s expedited-freight division, arranging urgent and time-sensitive shipments using straight trucks, box trucks, cargo vans and other equipment.
Edge Logistics , headquartered in Chicago, was founded in 2014. The logistics provider has around 120 employees, according to Built In Chicago .
Bountiful, Utah-based Freight Tec Management Group is a privately held freight brokerage founded in 1997. The company provides truckload, less-than-truckload and expedited freight services through a network of independent freight agents. Freight Tec has between 51 and 200 employees, according to LinkedIn .
Edge alleges the employees had access to confidential customer information, including shipping rates, pricing strategies, freight lanes, customer preferences and business relationships.
Rather than leave Edge and independently establish competing businesses, the employees allegedly worked with Freight Tec to develop a plan to transfer existing Edge accounts to the rival brokerage.
The lawsuit alleges that Freight Tec’s leadership knew the employees were subject to restrictive employment agreements and reviewed those agreements before engaging them.
Edge claims in court filings that Freight Tec’s CEO met with Daglas approximately three to five times before the employees departed to discuss their agreements, paperwork and the legality of their planned business arrangements.
The employees allegedly agreed to operate through independent agency businesses under Freight Tec’s brokerage authority, receiving a share of gross profits generated by the customers they brought to the company.
Three of the defendants established limited liability companies in April, according to the complaint:
Apiquian registered Freight Redefined LLC in Florida on April 20.
Harlan registered Thorndale Logistics LLC in Illinois on April 22.
Daglas registered Parlay Expedited LLC in Illinois on April 23.
Edge alleges all three companies were established while their owners were still employed by the brokerage.
The complaint further alleges the employees staggered their resignations to conceal the coordinated nature of their departure .
Daglas submitted his resignation May 8, telling Edge he was stepping away from the freight industry to focus on family, according to the lawsuit.
Harlan allegedly told colleagues he was leaving to work for a friend in Las Vegas, while Apiquian said he wanted a local, office-based position.
Edge claims those explanations concealed plans to continue working in freight brokerage through Freight Tec.
Customer emails allegedly established before departures
Among the lawsuit’s most detailed allegations are descriptions of customer-specific Freight Tec email accounts appearing in Edge shipment communications before the employees left the company.
On May 9, while Daglas and Hersh were still employed by Edge, an email account associated with Freight Tec and dedicated to an Edge customer identified as Customer A appeared in a shipment-related email thread, according to the complaint.
Five days later, on May 14, a second Freight Tec email account dedicated to Customer B appeared in a rate-request thread involving Daglas and Harlan’s Edge email addresses.
Edge contends those communications demonstrate that the defendants were preparing to service existing Edge customers through Freight Tec before their employment ended.
The complaint also describes subsequent transactions allegedly involving the same customers.
On June 28-29, Apiquian allegedly arranged an expedited shipment for Customer B through Freight Tec and Freight Redefined LLC, identifying himself as Freight Tec’s key accounts manager.
Hersh, identified in the complaint as a Freight Tec strategic account manager, allegedly coordinated delivery and confirmed the shipment’s final rate.
On Aug. 18, a representative of Customer A requested a transportation quote from Apiquian at his Freight Tec email address, with an Edge email address also included in the correspondence, according to the lawsuit.
Apiquian allegedly responded with a freight rate.
Edge also claims freight postings appeared on a load board for lanes previously handled by its brokerage, using Freight Tec addresses associated with Daglas and Harlan.
Alleged kickbacks funded by inflated freight rates
The complaint includes a separate allegation that former Edge employees arranged to pay kickbacks to a shipping customer’s decision-maker in exchange for directing freight to Freight Tec.
According to the lawsuit, the arrangement developed around April 2026, when representatives associated with a customer identified only as Customer C visited Chicago.
Edge alleges that the former employees informed an East Coast contact at Customer C about their plans to establish a competing operation through Freight Tec.
The customer contact allegedly agreed to direct shipments to the new operation but demanded kickbacks financed by adding money to freight charges.
The complaint alleges the defendants subsequently handled Customer C freight under that arrangement.
Edge contends the alleged payments gave Freight Tec an improper competitive advantage by influencing the customer’s freight-routing decisions rather than winning business through pricing or service.
The complaint does not identify Customer C, specify the amount of any alleged payments or include underlying invoices or payment records establishing the alleged kickbacks.
The allegations have not been proven in court.
Edge seeks injunction, damages and return of confidential information
Edge’s lawsuit contains 11 counts, including breach of contract, breach of duty of loyalty, tortious interference with contractual and prospective business relationships, aiding and abetting, civil conspiracy and unfair competition.
The company alleges the employees violated employment agreements containing confidentiality, noncompetition and nonsolicitation provisions.
Edge is asking the court to prohibit the defendants from using or disclosing its confidential business information and to restrict certain competitive activities and customer solicitation.
The company also seeks the return of confidential documents and electronic information, preservation and forensic imaging of electronic devices and accounts, monetary damages, disgorgement of allegedly improper profits and attorneys’ fees.
The complaint does not specify a dollar amount in damages.
Court documents indicate that attorneys for Daglas and Harlan previously challenged the enforceability of certain employment agreements, arguing that the agreements lacked sufficient consideration.
The complaint also acknowledges that Daglas’ employment agreement contains an arbitration provision. Edge says it is seeking injunctive relief against him in federal court at this stage and intends to pursue monetary claims through arbitration, subject to circumstances described in the complaint.
No court has ruled on the merits of Edge’s allegations or determined whether the disputed employment restrictions are enforceable.
Former employees have until Dec. 1 to respond
The four former employees and three related LLCs waived formal service of the complaint, according to court records filed Oct. 6.
Their responses to the lawsuit are due Dec. 1.
An initial status hearing is scheduled for Dec. 2 in Chicago.
As of the latest docket reviewed by FreightWaves, no defendant had filed a substantive response to the complaint, and the court had not issued a ruling on Edge’s allegations.
Why it matters: The Edge Logistics LLC v. Freight Tec Management Group Inc. case highlights the legal and financial risks freight brokers face when employees leave with valuable customer relationships and establish competing operations.

1968 Dodge Coronet Parked for Decades Gets Second Chance, It's a Rare R/T Convertible
13 photos
Photo: Steve Magnante/YouTube
Originally introduced as a full-size car in 1949, the Dodge Coronet was discontinued after 10 years on the market. It returned in 1965, but it was repositioned as an intermediate model. The Coronet was the brand's bread-and-butter mid-size car throughout the 1960s, as well as the base for the Charger and Super Bee muscle cars.
But while it may be overshadowed by the latter, the Coronet was an integral part of the muscle car wars. When ordered in two-door body styles, it was available with the same high-performance engines as the Charger and Super Bee, including the mighty 426-cubic-inch (7.0-liter) Hemi V8.
Moreover, and this is a fact that many people miss, it was Dodge's first vehicle to sport the R/T emblem. Although the badge is more commonly associated with the Charger, the Coronet was the first to get it. Dodge introduced the Coronet R/T in 1967, a full year before the Charger.
The R/T stood for Road and Track and hinted that the said Coronet was also suitable for racing. Dodge likely had the drag strip in mind. Unlike the standard Coronet or the 500 version, the R/T came standard with the 440-cubic-inch (7.2-liter) V8 , rated at 375 horsepower. The Hemi was optional. The Charger R/T arrived in 1968 with similar specs.
While the Coronet was a hot seller, the R/T version brought notably fewer customers into showrooms. In 1967, only 10,809 of the around 180,000 units sold were R/Ts (about 6%). In 1968, production remained similar at 10,849 examples (out of 196,000 units—5.5%). Sales dropped to 7,200 units in 1969 (4.1%) and 2,615 examples in 1970 (2.3%).
The Hemi version is obviously the rarest. Dodge sold fewer than 1,400 units between 1966 and 1970. About half of them were delivered in 1966, when the R/T wasn't available. So we're actually looking at only 637 examples with both the R/T and Hemi. But the convertible body style is also pretty rare.
Combining the retractable top and the Hemi gives us outstandingly low numbers , but the drop-top alone is scarce in R/T format. Only 1,760 rolled off the assembly line over four model years, most of them equipped with the four-barrel 440 V8. The derelict convertible you see here is one of those cars.
Found by classic car enthusiast Steve Magnante somewhere in Massachusetts, this Mopar is one of nearly 11,000 Coronet R/Ts sold in 1968. However, the convertible body style narrows that number to only 519 examples. The car was born with the three-speed automatic, and existing records say that 423 units were built in this exact drivetrain configuration.
It's quite the rare Mopar, but it's also in pretty bad shape. Based on the amount of rust covering the body, this Coronet spent a few good decades off the road. In fact, I'm pretty sure that it sat under full exposure to the elements. Some of the interior was gutted, while the original V8 engine is no longer under the hood.
The car still has a 440 V8 in the bay, but it appears to be incorrect for the model year. The tall valve covers hint at a 1970s version of the RB mill. It also includes a few other day-two mods .
While much of the red interior is still around to tell its story, the exterior color is a mystery. I've seen traces of Plum Crazy purple on the firewall, but Dodge did not offer this hue at the time. The floor panels show metallic blue, which was a factory option. On the flipside, it's a rather strange choice for a red interior.
However, I also noticed a bit of red paint on the door jambs, and a red-on-red layout would make sense. Or perhaps the white that still covers some section of the trunk may have something to do with the original finish.
Anyway, while this Coronet may look too far gone, someone decided to give it a second chance. One of the rear fenders was already replaced, while the other one was cut off for similar treatment. Steve says that the Coronet will be restored, which is terrific news for such a rare Mopar. But it may take a while until we see it back on the road.

source_document.body:
US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth speaks at the Association of the United States Army (AUSA) 2026 Annual Meeting and Exposition in Washington, DC on October 14, 2026. The AUSA Meeting and Exposition is a defense trade show and networking event for the global defense community. (Photo by Jim WATSON / AFP via Getty Images)
WASHINGTON — Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and service leaders took center stage at the Association of the US Army’s annual conference this morning discussing broad plans to scale autonomous weapons and stand up a new four-star command.
“You have autonomy. You have robotics. You have SI [super intelligence]. You have space,” Hegseth told an audience full of servicemembers and industry figures. “It’s that the folks who acquire it [defense platforms] need to be right there, up with the warfighter at the same time, who understand how to iterate it and change on and innovate on it.”
While Hegseth and service civilian leader steered clear of many specifics about autonomy development and investment plans today, they used the event to discuss the need to stand up the recently announced Autonomous Warfare Command , or AUTOWARCOM, that is envisioned as having service-like authorities to scale autonomous and robotic capabilities across the joint force.
While Congress will have to sign off on the plan — a move that could take time— the Defense Department is moving out with several efforts to pave that path forward. For instance, the Pentagon has shifted the Direct Reporting Portfolio Manager (DRPM) for autonomy into an umbrella unmanned tech initiative called Project Agincourt.
Owen West , who is now leading that project, moderated today’s AUSA autonomy panel that provided some insight into management changes, including to the Defense Autonomous Working Group (DAWG).
DAWG was established as follow-on to the Biden-era Replicator initiative to dramatically increase the production of drones and counter-drone tech. In 2025 DAWG was placed under Special Operations Command (SOCOM) with the goal of focusing on different capability portfolios.
“We’re smaller. We’re able to iterate at the speed of relevancy,” said Derrick Anderson, the assistant secretary of defense for Special Operations and Low-Intensity Conflict.
Anderson said now DAWG is being absorbed by a new Task Force Autonomous Warfare inside SOCOM to support Project Agincourt and, eventually, AUTOWARCOM, to “keep iterating” inside the autonomy space and so that there isn’t a “stagnant pause.”
“Our guys are going to keep pushing forward,” Anderson added.
While lawmakers have not yet approved a fiscal 2027 defense spending bill or moved ahead with the administration’s separate reconciliation request, the Pentagon has laid out plans to spend nearly $55 billion on DAWG.
It remains unclear how much of that request will ultimately be approved by Congress, but Hegseth reiterated this morning that the full request is necessary to “drive change” inside the department.
“[It is] a one-time generational investment gives us a chance to reflect the president’s priorities,” Hegseth said on stage.
“Investments now are going to matter, and they’re going to ripple not just for years but for decades across our joint force,” he later added.

Networking
STH AWS Networking Lab Tour - Hollow core fiber model with air center channel
AWS invited us to tour the networking lab where it develops its own switches, timing appliances, optical modules, and fiber connectors. We flew out to an unmarked building a few weeks ago, where Sam and I got out of the car wondering if we had the correct address. The tour covered switch generations from 3.2Tbps to 102.4Tbps, hardware encryption at line rate, a private time distribution network accurate to 20 microseconds, DWDM modules that put 64 wavelengths on one fiber strand, hollow-core fiber with roughly 33 percent better latency, connectors that install 64 fibers in about one second, and even a molded cover for ganged fibers that acts as a dust cover and loopback.
Since Sam and I had to fly to the lab and AWS covered our travel expenses, we have to say this is sponsored. Also, since it was a lab tour, we were asked not to film many things, and there are others covered in the background. I asked AWS to review the footage to ensure we were not disclosing anything unintended. Since some items the reviewers did not know AWS planned to disclose, we will use only frames from the approved video footage for this release. Make no mistake, there is a lot of new stuff in the video that you will not have seen elsewhere, and if you are into networking, timing, and hyperscale, it is probably the most interesting video of 2026. Certainly share it with your colleagues.
AWS Switching to 102.4Tbps
The first bench holds the AWS in-house switch family, spanning several generations. Some of what we will show you are silver, unpainted lab chassis. I asked about the coloring, and apparently it seems to align with the Pantone color of the year. The blue chassis is a 3.2 Tbps switch with 32 QSFP28 ports at 100GbE each. It is already an older design at this point, and you can see that from inside.
STH AWS Networking Lab Tour – Blue 3.2 Tbps AWS switch with cover removed
The green box next to it is the current volume deployment, a 12.8 Tbps switch where every port has moved from 100G QSFP28 to 400G QSFP-DD. This is also the generation that moved signaling from NRZ to PAM4.
STH AWS Networking Lab Tour – Inside the green 12.8 Tbps AWS switch
Opening the chassis makes the power increase obvious. The ASIC gets a larger heatsink, and the QSFP56 cages get their own larger heatsinks as well. Inside there is an Annapurna Labs management processor and an SSD for logging.
A small board with a big job
AWS pointed out one small internal board as a key part of reliability in the newer switches and optical modules. The board communicates with every pluggable optics module over I2C and collects telemetry, so operators can identify a failing module before it affects its neighbors.
STH AWS Networking Lab Tour – I2C telemetry board inside the AWS switch
We were told this board may look like an ordinary PCB, but inside AWS it counts as a major innovation because of the telemetry information it provides and how it accomplishes that.
AWS 51.2Tbps with 800G OSFP ports
AWS is deploying the 51.2 Tbps generation heavily at the time of filming. The front panel carries OSFP ports running PAM4-112 SerDes, which gives 800GbE per port. For STH readers, Octal for eight, then 112G for roughly 100Gbps per lane.
STH AWS Networking Lab Tour – OSFP 800G ports on the 51.2 Tbps AWS switch
The heatsink grows again because two copies of the I2C telemetry board sit under it alongside the switch ASIC. The rear holds the management processor, power distribution and fan control. Chassis colors track generations in this lab. Blue covers the 3.2T, green covers the 12.8T, and we were told this one is officially peach.
102.4 Tbps with 1.6T ports
The next step up runs at 102.4 Tbps and is not in volume deployment yet. AWS says it will roll out over the coming quarters and years. Each OSFP port uses PAM4-224 SerDes for a raw 1.6 Tbps. That is sixteen times the per-port bandwidth of the blue switch, on twice as many ports, so cooling grows accordingly.
STH AWS Networking Lab Tour – OSFP 1.6T ports on the 102.4 Tbps AWS switch
At these speeds, the optical modules include their own built-in cooling, which we have seen on other platforms at this performance level. Production units are expected in a whitish color, completing a palette of blue, green, peach and white.
STH AWS Networking Lab Tour – Inside the 102.4 Tbps AWS switch
You can also see the management, I2C, and SSD logging in here, with the power delivery becoming more robust.
Encryption at line rate
The last switch on the bench handles a different problem. Every port on this 12.8 Tbps unit encrypts traffic, on the reasoning that data leaving a data center should be encrypted by default. The same chassis also serves as long-haul equipment because its ports accept high-power 400ZR optics, so coherent modules can plug straight in and drive fiber over metro distances.
STH AWS Networking Lab Tour – Encrypted 12.8 Tbps Maxx switch front panel
Sixteen FPGAs handle encryption at line rate, which explains the two-rack-unit chassis. More silicon means more power and more cooling.
STH AWS Networking Lab Tour – Inside the encrypted 12.8 Tbps switch
A neat one here is that the Annapurna Labs management processor is mounted flipped relative to the other designs on the bench. You can also see the I2C board and the logging SSD here.
The management network
AWS also builds its own 1GbE management switch. A 1GbE switch is not exotic, but AWS told us that the management plane is what makes a large network operable at their scale.
STH AWS Networking Lab Tour – AWS custom 1GbE management switch front panel
The board carries PHYs, transformers, a switch chip, a management processor and a logging SSD. It is the same architecture as the high-speed boxes at far lower bandwidth.
STH AWS Networking Lab Tour – Inside the AWS 1GbE management switch with PHYs and SSD
Alongside it sits an AWS-built serial console server. Yes, AWS even designed its own console server.
STH AWS Networking Lab Tour – AWS serial console server with cover removed
Whatever else changes in the network, out-of-band access still runs on 1970s-era serial technology.
A separate timing network
The appliance on the next stand keeps time across fleets of hundreds of thousands of servers. Satellites provide reference clocks, and AWS distributes a pulse-per-second signal downstream over a dedicated timing network that is independent of its data and management networks.
STH AWS Networking Lab Tour – AWS timing appliance front panel with antenna inputs
The front panel resembles a 48-port SFP switch, but these ports do not run Ethernet. The time distribution protocol is proprietary to AWS. Multiple antenna inputs provide redundancy. Four ports face upstream, and the rest face downstream so the network can be built as a tree that reaches every device. AWS then needs a map of the tree, plus the cable lengths and speeds of each link, to calibrate timing for each device.
Accurate time matters for ordering. Distributed databases need write timestamps to guarantee that reads return current data, and log analysis is only as reliable as its clock sources. Standard NTP delivers roughly 500 microseconds of accuracy. AWS claims its timing infrastructure guarantees time to within 20 microseconds, and we were told that figure is conservative.
STH AWS Networking Lab Tour – Inside the AWS timing appliance
Inside the appliance, two FPGAs monitor the pluggables over I2C, and a third runs the proprietary timing logic. An SSD, an Annapurna Labs processor, power distribution, and a fan control board fill out the rest.
Next, let us get to optics, connectors, and a special part.

Posted By: Colin McClelland October 14, 2026
The global nickel market is heading for another surplus this year, reversing an earlier forecast for a shortage, the International Nickel Study Group says.
Production is forecast at 3.87 million tonnes against demand of 3.85 million tonnes in 2026, leaving a 19,000-tonne surplus. The excess is expected to widen to 70,000 tonnes next year, the Lisbon-based intergovernmental body said in its October outlook issued Tuesday.
“Nickel’s role in the battery market has also grown more gradually than anticipated,” the group said. “It faces competition from lithium iron phosphate chemistries.”
The reversal reflects a larger upward revision to expected supply than demand for the metal, widely used in stainless steel production and in electric vehicle batteries. INSG raised its production forecast by 153,000 tonnes and its consumption forecast by 102,000 tonnes from April, when it projected a deficit of 32,000 tonnes. April’s outlook had put production at 3.71 million tonnes and consumption at 3.74 million tonnes.
Output unchanged
This year’s expected surplus remains well below the 299,000 tonnes estimated for 2025. Demand is forecast to grow 7.6% this year while production is almost unchanged. In 2027, output is expected to reach 4.07 million tonnes against consumption of 4 million tonnes.
Indonesia’s expansion has reshaped nickel supply. Chinese-backed projects have increased their capacity to produce materials for stainless steel and batteries, INSG said in an earlier market review . The group estimated in October 2025 that Indonesia accounted for two-thirds of global nickel mine output that year.
Indonesia approved a significantly lower nickel ore mining quota for 2026 than for 2025, although permit holders could seek an upward revision subject to the government’s assessment of supply and demand, INSG said in April.
Canadian producers are also part of the supply picture. Vale (NYSE: VALE) reported 10,400 tonnes of finished nickel from its Voisey’s Bay operations in the second quarter, up 1,800 tonnes from a year earlier as underground ore output increased. Sudbury contributed 6,700 tonnes, down 1,900 tonnes because of planned maintenance, the company said in its production update .
Glencore (LSE: GLEN; JSE: GLN; ASX: GLC), whose nickel business includes operations in Canada and Australia, produced 35,800 tonnes from its own sources in the first half and maintained full-year guidance of 70,000 to 80,000 tonnes, it said in its half-year report .
The consequences of oversupply are visible at BHP (ASX, NYSE, LSE: BHP), whose remaining Western Australia Nickel assets are suspended. The company agreed this month to sell its Kambalda nickel concentrator to Gold Fields (NYSE, JSE: GFI)and plans to review the wider suspension by February 2027, considering options including a restart, further asset sales or closure, BHP said in an Oct. 7 statement .
Stainless steel provides a source of demand growth. Global output rose 5% to about 33 million tonnes in the first half, the Brussels-based World Stainless Association said in an August release . Asian production increased 6.1%, while European Union output fell 3.7%.
Battery competition
Lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries accounted for more than 55% of global electric vehicle battery deployment in 2025, up from nearly 50% a year earlier, the Paris-based International Energy Agency said in its EV outlook for this year. The chemistry offers an alternative to nickel-bearing batteries.
The shift remains uneven. Nearly 80% of EV batteries deployed outside China last year used nickel-containing chemistries, the agency said.
INSG cautioned that its forecasts remain uncertain, particularly for Indonesian production, and don’t include an allowance for possible production disruptions.

Gen. Ronald P. Clark Commanding General United States Army Pacific (USARPAC), delivers a presentation on "Land Forces: The Foundation of Pacific Stability" during the first day of the annual Maneuver Warfighter Conference Sept. 15, 2026, in Marshall Auditorium at Fort Benning, Georgia. The annual Maneuver Warfighter Conference gathers U.S. Army senior leaders and subject-matter experts from across the globe to discuss the way forward for maneuver forces. (U.S. Army photo by Daniel Marble)
WASHINGTON — The current continuing resolution (CR) is the “biggest challenge” the Army’s Pacific Command (USARPAC) is facing, as it prevents the force from getting new capabilities for its unified network and long-range precision fires, its four-star commander said.
“That’s the biggest challenge. It’s plans for new starts and being able to fund some of the programs that we know are going to yield benefit to the soldier on the ground,” Gen. Ronald Clark told re porters Tuesday w hen asked how the delayed passing of the fiscal 2027 budget is affecting operations in the region.
Clark did not mention specific new start programs that would be affected, but said many of the programs relate to “some of the experimentation that we’re doing” with the Mission Partner Network (MPN). MPN is what the Army describes as a “unified system” where the joint force, partners and allies can share information. He added that one of the new start programs for the MPN is a “piece of equipment,” but declined to comment further.
Clark also said that there are additional capabilities that are “currently” in development and need to continue to develop “specific to long-range precision fires” that are cheaper and can be built more quickly than current capabilities. Such fires capabilities are something the command needs “in order to remain the most lethal land force on [the] face of the Earth,” Clark said.
The Defense Department as a whole has more than 150 new start programs in its 2027 budget, with at least 29 of those deriving from the Army, Breaking Defense reported . To reach this number, Breaking Defense searched both the procurement budget and research, development, test and evaluation budget documents for the phrase “new start.”
Breaking Defense reached out to the Pentagon and the serv ices at the time to a sk for details on new starts that will be impacted by the CR, but a list was not provided.
Though Clark would not provide specifics about which new start pertaining to long range precision fires USARPAC was waiting on, the service included a new start of $921.9 million for Terminal High Altitude Aerial Defense along with $132.1 million for the AN/TPY-2 sensor, which serves as the “brain and eyes” for the THAAD system, in its budget request. Breaking Defense could not identify any MPN programs in the 2027 budget documents.
“It’s a challenge, again, we have to overcome, but it’s part of the fiscal environment,” Clark said. “We have more experience operating under CR than we do with an appropriation.”

Harley-Davidson Shadow Rider Carries Lord of the Rings Elvish Markings
38 photos
Photo: Thunderbike
Years upon years of covering custom Harley-Davidson motorcycles have me convinced that, if you really stretch your imagination, you can liken a Breakout 117 cruiser to anything you like. I must admit, though, I wasn’t really expecting someone to incorporate Tolkien’s Lord of the Rings trilogy into one.
Yet here it is, a Breakout conversion handled by German custom garage Thunderbike for an unnamed Italian customer. The reference to The Lord of the Rings is not that visible, true, as it only manifests itself as a small vignette with Elvish lettering, but even that’s enough to give the build a certain aura of mystery.
Other than that, the build is the usual conversion of a Breakout into something else. The first things that had to go were the wheels, which have been replaced by something called the Vegas Cut.
Made in-house by Thunderbike, the wheels come in ten spokes, grouped in pairs of two, with a completely black (high-gloss black, that is) look to them. The wheel at the front comes in at 21 inches across, while the rear one measures 18 inches.
The fitting of the modified wheels created the need for other components of the motorcycle to be replaced or upgraded. The Germans installed a wave brake disc at the front, measuring an impressive 340 mm in diameter and requiring special caliper adapters.
Other mildly mechanical changes include the lowering of the fork, the fitting of a pulley, and a swingarm conversion that contributes to making the 260 mm wide rear wheel visible in all of its glory.
The fenders pulled over the two wheels are aftermarket as well, with the one at the front a slim metal piece, and the one at the rear integrating the bike’s stop lights and turn signals. In between the two fenders, right behind the fuel tank, Thunderbike fitted a Spirit Leather seat with a honeycomb structure.
There are a wealth of minor but impactful changes made to the Breakout so that it could become the Shadow Rider, as it’s now called. That includes the fitting of a headlamp cap that supposedly gives the two-wheeler an evil look (I don’t really see that), the installation of a spoiler, and swapping the handlebar, grips, and mirrors for custom parts. Thunderbike also had a say in the way the footpegs now present themselves.
When all the changes have been completed, the German shop opted to paint everything black, including the visible components of the Milwaukee-Eight engine that sits unmodified in the Softail frame.
The cost of the project is not a public matter, but Thunderbike has this habit of listing the cost of the parts it used to make a custom motorcycle. And in this case, they amount to around $13,000.

CuMo is located inside the Boise National Forest in southwestern Idaho. Credit: U.S. Forest Service/Wikimedia Commons
Posted By: Blair McBride October 14, 2026
An updated preliminary economic assessment (PEA) for Idaho Copper’s (NYSE-A: COPR) CuMo copper-molybdenum-silver project gives it a 46-year life and improves some economics from a previous study but it still carries significant costs and a modest rate of return.
Discounted at 8%, the update more than quadruples CuMo’s post-tax net present value (NPV) to $1.8 billion (C$2.6 billion) over the 2020 PEA, while initial capital costs fell by 62% to $1.1 billion, the company reported Wednesday. The post-tax internal rate of return (IRR) doubled to 18.5%. CuMo is about 60 km northeast of state capital Boise.
“This is a very different project from the one that was described in 2020,” Idaho Copper CEO Andrew Brodkey said in a release on Wednesday.
Processing cuts costs
“Starting with a smaller plant and sorting the ore before it reaches the mill means we need materially less capital up front, with a rapid payback driven by ore sorting. Very few copper projects anywhere combine returns at this level with such a strong mine life, and fewer still sit in the United States and carry molybdenum, rhenium and tungsten alongside the copper.”
The updated assessment comes as the U.S. seeks to expand domestic production of critical minerals and reduce its reliance on foreign suppliers, potentially giving projects such as CuMo strategic importance beyond their financial returns.
Idaho Copper shares fell 4% to $3 apiece in New York on Wednesday morning, valuing the company at $56.3 million (C$81 million). The stock has traded in a 12-month range of $2.05 to $18.
In addition to the initial capital costs, the PEA update envisions staged development at CuMo, with an expansion in operations in year five that’s expected to cost $658 million to raise the mine’s capacity.
41M lb copper
CuMo could produce 41.6 million lb. of copper, 30.5 million lb. of molybdenum and 1.3 million oz. of silver annually in the project’s first 21 years. It has a payback period of 5.9 years, according to the update.
The study assumes substantially higher metal prices than in the 2020 PEA. The copper and molybdenum prices gained 66% to $5 per lb. and $25 per lb., respectively, and silver increased by about 186% to $50 per ounce.
CuMo hosts 2.2 billion measured and indicated tons grading 0.08% copper, 0.05% molybdenum, and 2.5 grams silver per tonne for 3.8 billion lb. contained copper, 1.5 billion lb. molybdenum and 165.5 million oz. silver, according to the 2020 PEA. Inferred resources total 2.5 billion inferred tons at 0.06% copper, 0.04% molybdenum, and 2.1 grams silver for 3.4 billion lb. contained copper, 1.4 billion lb. molybdenum and 158.8 million oz. silver. Idaho Copper plans to work on a prefeasibility in 2027, targeted for completion in 2028, Brodkey said.

Mazda has little in the way of experience with electric vehicles. The limited-run Demio EV and the MX-30 EV come to mind. Mazda followed up with the 6e fastback sedan and CX-6e crossover, which shouldn't be viewed as thoroughbreds because of Changan's engineering and manufacturing involvement. Moving forward, the automaker's next electric model is expected to debut the Skyactiv EV Scalable Architecture.
Our spy photographers may have caught a mule of said model, but looking more closely at it and its surroundings, the development vehicle may not be a Mazda at all. The mule in question may belong to British automaker Jaguar Land Rover, which is only natural to assume when you see a highly secret Mazda development vehicle entering JLR's facility at the Nurburgring.
That uncertainty makes it all the more difficult to guess what is actually hiding under the CX-90 body panels, with the mule showing different proportions from those of the production CX-90. Retaining much of the donor's sheet metal, the front wheels sit awkwardly far behind the original wheel wells.
We can further spot a shorter wheelbase, a rear overhang that has been cut down, and narrower tracks. A conspicuous front overhang makes identification all the more difficult, but said front end offers a glimpse of the battery housing. Based on how crude this fellow is, the final design should be vastly different.
Its nose has been covered up as well, showing a small cooling intake right below the grille area. That arrangement also confirms an electric powertrain, which features distinct cooling requirements from an internal combustion engine like the four- and six-cylinder mills of the CX-90 and lesser CX-70.
Photo: SH Proshots The mismatched wheels and body panels are further signs that all of its body serves as a temporary shell, with either Mazda or Jaguar Land Rover testing the underpinnings of what sport utility vehicle they may be planning next. The question is, why would Jaguar Land Rover use a CX-90 body to disguise a more compact sport utility vehicle than the Defender and Range Rover Sport?
We all know that JLR has a couple of new models in the offing, including a smaller Defender and a replacement for the Velar. Based on the EMA platform rather than the MLA of the Range Rover Sport Electric, the Range Rover GT does not serve as the successor to the internal combustion Velar. Instead, the folks at JLR describe it as the fifth member of the upscale Range Rover family.
Having cleared that up, borrowing an unrelated shell can easily conceal the eventual design while allowing real-world testing to begin. The result can look ridiculous, but that is certainly the point of a mule. Styling is completely irrelevant during the phase when engineers are focused on the mechanical side of the development process, with test mules allowing engineers to evaluate the platform, suspension, battery packaging, and everything in between.
A makeshift CX-90 entering a JLR facility near a German circuit is not conclusive proof of either a Jaguar Land Rover design or a Mazda design. Mazda does have a dedicated electric vehicle program that will hopefully right the wrongs of the MX-30 EV. While not a false start, the MX-30 EV simply wasn't convincing enough as an electric vehicle and as a sport utility vehicle.
The first in-house Mazda electric vehicle after the MX-30 EV is now anticipated in late 2028 or early 2029 , and its platform supports a variety of battery chemistries and body styles. Integrated vehicle control systems would also seek to reproduce the responsive driving character Mazda associates with its Jinba Ittai philosophy.

New Lamborghini Fountain Pens and Rollerballs Made by Montegrappa to Hit the Market in November
33 photos
Photo: Montegrappa
There is almost nothing in this world, no object or idea, that can’t be tied one way or another to the world of the automobile. From clothes to spaceships, one can put an automotive twist on absolutely anything. Like, say, a new collection of fountain pens and rollerballs.
Not being into luxury pens and other such writing instruments, I have to admit I don’t get all that many chances to write about Montegrappa . Yet, now I kind of have to, as Italy’s oldest player in this industry just came out with a new line of products dedicated to the Lamborghini Miura.
Generally regarded as the world's first true supercar, the Italian mechanical masterpiece has long sung its final song, but that doesn’t mean it completely disappeared from people’s minds. In fact, it is this exact model that has inspired a collection called Automobili Lamborghini Miura: Lines in Lasting Motion.
Put together by Montegrappa and the Italian carmaker, the limited-edition collection of writing instruments is meant to celebrate this historically important vehicle exactly 60 years after it first came to market. And by celebrate I don’t mean they carry tribute stickers and markings, but they actually incorporate some of the car’s main design lines, while at the same time reinterpreting them.
Supposedly, it all starts with the silhouette of the pens, which try to recall Miura’s bodywork lines, while at the same time giving that a more modern twist. The end cap, for instance, is meant to remind us of the iconic black louvred rear window engine cover, something specialists refer to as the Venetian grille.
The pens also carry the shield of the Sant’ Agata Bolognese-based carmaker, and their caps feature a rock crystal that’s placed on an engraved base to mimic the retractable headlight of the car. To further accentuate this connection, the cap features a complicated tactile push-button mechanism that, when engaged, mimics the headlight movement of the Miura.
As said, this is a luxury pen I’m talking about, and, as such, it incorporates an abundance of precious materials. There is 18-karat and ruthenium plating on the nib, engraved with the Lambo shield and matched by an ebonite feeder.
Montegrappa said it would be making 60 pens and an equal number of rollerballs as part of this collection, and that it would offer them in three colors, they too inspired by the hues available for the Miura : Fly Yellow, Miura Green, and Black.
Each pen is to be delivered in its own custom packaging, made to resemble the interior of the Lamborghini vehicle. They will become available for collectors and enthusiasts in mid-November, for prices that have not been disclosed.
For the record, this is not the first time Montegrappa and Lamborghini jointly developed something. Three years ago, when the Raging Bull was celebrating its own 60th anniversary, the pen maker launched its first dedicated collection, made in ultra-light aluminum, forged carbon, and titanium, and carrying the same 18k gold nib. For perspective, those pens sold back then for around $6,500.

Tesla Left Intriguing Hints in the Roadster Demo Confirmation, Here's How To Watch the Livestream
6 photos
Photo: Tesla
Tesla appears to keep its promise about the Roadster demonstration on October 15, confirming the livestream at 7:55 PM CST. The time is another nod to the Back to the Future movies, with Musk pointing to it with a "Timing is everything" tweet. Based on a NOTAM filed with the FAA, SpaceX closed the space around its Waco, TX, testing facility on Wednesday, supposedly to rehearse the demo.
Among all the promises Elon Musk and Tesla made, the Roadster has been the most controversial. Announced in 2017 as a "one more thing" during the Tesla Semi launch, the Roadster 2.0 should've started production in 2020. The pandemic certainly muddied the waters, but the Roadster soon became an afterthought, and soon after that Tesla stopped considering itself a carmaker.
Elon Musk's company has since abandoned several car projects, including an affordable compact and the successors to the Model S and Model X. However, it never quite gave up on the Roadster, insisting that it's still on the roadmap, with solid plans to produce it. That was a small consolation for those who paid a $50,000 deposit for the Roadster, not to mention those who paid the full $250,000 price for a Founder Edition model.
Earlier this year, Tesla announced an epic Roadster demo on October 1, which was later postponed to October 15 due to adverse weather conditions. One day before the new schedule, Tesla confirmed that the Roadster demo would, indeed, take place on October 15 at 7:55 PM CST. The time is significant, something Elon Musk was quick to emphasize in a post on Twitter.
Similar to the "Where we're going" easter egg in the original teaser image, the time of the livestream is a direct reference to the Back to the Future movie. I'm not a fan of the series, but according to some, 7:55 PM, or rather 19:55, is a nod to 1955, the year Marty goes back in the movie. According to others, 7:55 is also the time shown in the opening scene of the Back to the Future movie.
Others believe that 7:55, together with Musk's specific use of words ( "Timing is everything" ), might indicate that the Roadster could complete a quarter mile in 7.55 seconds. The fastest production vehicle is currently the Rimac Nevera R, which does the quarter mile in 7.90 seconds. If the 7.55 estimate is right, it would make the Tesla Roadster the fastest production vehicle.
Regardless of these speculations, Tesla fans fully expect the Roadster to fly or at least hover during the October 15 demo event. If Tesla delivers less than that, the electric sports car is doomed before even starting production. Which, based on conservative estimates, should not happen for at least another year, if ever.
Still, the Roadster demo remains the most exciting Tesla event in years, and everyone is eager to watch it live. Tesla will livestream it on X starting at 7:55 PM CST on October 15. This translates to 8:55 PM EDT and 5:55 PM PDT. Europeans would be able to tune in on October 16 at 1:55 AM (UK/GMT) and 2:55 AM CEST (Central Europe). Similarly, people in Asia could watch the livestream on October 16, from 8:55 AM (China) and 9:55 AM (Japan). Timing is everything — Elon Musk (@elonmusk) October 14, 2026

By Alison Koo
14 October 2026
Missiles struck two container ships in Global Feeder Shipping’s (GFS) fleet in the Strait of Hormuz in the last 24 hours, with one vessel subsequently sinking after catching fire.
Singapore’s Maritime and Port Authority (MPA) said that the 2008-built 2,824 teu GFS Pride was damaged and caught fire before sinking. All of its 21 crewmen were evacuated, with no injuries reported.
The other ship, 2015-built 4,350 teu GFS Giselle, sustained hull damage but remained operational and proceeded under its own power to a safe anchorage. All 22 crew members were safe, and no injuries were reported.
Both ships are Singapore-flagged but had no Singaporeans among their crew.
SeaSearcher’s AIS data shows that GFS Pride was approximately one nautical mile east of Ras Makhbuq, Oman, when it was hit.
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy said an unnamed container ship carrying more than 2,500 containers had struck a mine while transiting what it described as an “unauthorised and dangerous” route through the strait.
The sinking of GFS Pride is the second vessel loss since the US-Israel-Iran war began on 28 February, according to data from the International Maritime Organization, the United Nations’ shipping agency. The earlier incident involved a bulk carrier, Cape Dao, which sank in the Gulf of Oman yesterday, after being hit by two torpedoes on 23 September. One Indian seafarer was killed and two others were injured.
Both GFS Pride and GFS Giselle were originally owned by Dubai-based Simatech Shipping, before the latter’s liner operations were acquired by GFS in October 2018. Abu Dhabi-based AD Ports owns 81% of GFS.
GFS’ website states that GFS Pride served a Khor Fakkan-Fujairah-Karachi service, and was supposed to have arrived in Khor Fakkan on Friday. GFS Giselle is deployed on a Fujairah-Khor Fakkan-India (Nhava Sheva) service and was due to have arrived in Khor Fakkan, also on Friday.
MPA said it was in contact with the vessels’ management company and was closely monitoring developments.
The authority expressed concern over continued attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, including the latest incidents involving the two Singapore-registered ships.
It described the attacks as unprovoked and unjustifiable, saying they violated international law.
MPA added that all actions affecting international shipping must comply with international law, particularly the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, and must not jeopardise the safety of vessels or seafarers.

Repeated Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia’s airports and energy infrastructure have sharply escalated the Saudi-Houthi conflict, raising the prospect of renewed disruption to Red Sea shipping as the 2027 contract-tendering season gets underway.
Saudi Arabia has vowed a “serious response” after strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport killed at least 14 people and injured more than 300. The airport remains closed until at least October 17, airlines have canceled flights, and the Houthis have threatened further attacks on Saudi airports, and military targets. The Yemen-based militia overnight hit the headquarters of Aramco, the Saudi oil producer, with missiles.
The attacks follow Houthi attempts beginning in July to close the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to Saudi-linked traffic, including vessel attacks into August after nearly nine months of relative quiet. The ‘other’ Mideast strait guards the Red Sea’s southern entrance to the Gulf of Aden. The latest escalation increases the likelihood that Red Sea transits could again become more dangerous , although no broad closure of the waterway has been confirmed.
For container lines, the immediate effect is uncertainty rather than a confirmed capacity shock, said analyst and SONAR data contributor Freightos (NASDAQ: CRGO ). Carriers had gradually increased Asia-Europe transits through the Red Sea since June, helping expand effective vessel supply; a renewed wave of attacks could reverse that trend and support rates.
Asia-Europe Rates Still Elevated
Spot rates on Asia-Europe lanes have fallen steadily since July, driven primarily by the post-peak demand slowdown and by carriers’ gradual return to Red Sea routings. Yet prices remain well above year-ago levels: both major Asia-Europe trades were above $3,000 per FEU last week, roughly 70% higher than in October 2025.
Some carriers have already announced October general rate increases. Asia-Mediterranean spot prices rose 7% to $3,800 per FEU last week, a move that could help establish a higher benchmark ahead of annual contract negotiations .
The market’s underlying support is fragile. Lingering congestion in Northern Europe and the Far East has absorbed capacity, while a threatened German port strike that could have worsened European delays was recently averted.
Contract negotiations face uncertainty
Shippers and carriers are entering tendering season for 2027 annual contracts with conflicting signals. Carriers enter talks with rates still historically elevated, but there are reasons shippers may resist locking in current levels.
Newbuild deliveries expected next year would expand fleet capacity, while continued growth in Red Sea transits would further increase effective capacity by shortening Asia-Europe voyages. Those factors have led some shippers to expect rates to ease in 2027 and to hesitate over long-term commitments at present levels.
Trans-Pacific peak may be ending
The trans-Pacific trade has held near peak-season levels since July, supported by sustained demand and Asia congestion. But the first signs of easing are emerging: Far East-U.S West Coast rates dipped 2% to $8,150 per FEU, potentially signaling the start of a post-Golden Week decline.
The National Retail Federation’s latest U.S. import forecast points to a sharp seasonal slowdown, projecting November ocean arrivals to fall 11% month over month. Even so, full-year 2026 imports are projected to be just 1.4% above 2025 and 1.2% above 2024, approaching the record volume set in 2021.
Outlook
Rates may continue to soften through the remainder of the quarter as peak-season cargo tapers. The principal upside risk is geopolitical: A sustained Houthi campaign against Saudi targets, or renewed attacks on commercial shipping in the Red Sea, could tighten effective capacity and complicate carriers’ efforts to defend rate levels heading into 2027 contract talks.

The 2027 Ford Bronco is not available with the 2.7-liter EcoBoost V6 that used to bridge the gap between the 2.3 and the 3.0 mills for model year 2026. In non-Raptor grades, the new midranger adds 50 horsepower and 25 pound-feet (34 Newton-meters) of twist over the 2.7 it replaces.
Beyond the discontinuation of the 2.7-liter EcoBoost V6, the Ford Motor Company has also removed the Stroppe Edition. The dealer order guide records a few interesting equipment changes. First and foremost, said order guide lists the 380-hp V6 as optional for the Outer Banks, Heritage, and four-door Badlands. It becomes standard on the new Filson specification.
Slotting below the punchier Raptor engine, the 3.0 introduced for 2027 makes a healthy 440 pound-feet (597 Newton-meters) at full chatter. That puts the lesser tune on the same level as the Raptor in terms of peak torque, but rubber, suspension, and setup continue to serve as differentiators.
Compared to the old 2.7 engine, the 3.0 should improve the driving experience in pretty much every imaginable scenario. Whether it's similarly efficient or a bit thirstier, the EPA will clarify that in due time. The 2.3-liter EcoBoost I4 remains the standard mill on the Base and Big Bend, manual and all. In two-pedal realm, automatic Broncos all feature 10-speed transmissions.
The new Filson grade receives the 3.0-liter engine as standard, leaning into a more tailored cabin full of leather and vinyl upholstery, complete with heated and ventilated front seats, power adjustment, and some distinctive trim here and there. The four-door Filson sweetens the deal with 35-inch tires and power running boards. Iron Sands and Field Green distinguish it from the rest of the range.
Photo: Ford To reach dealers in early 2027, the Filson will be joined by the RTR. Taking a completely different route, this fellow pairs the 2.3 with an anti-lag setup, upgraded cooling, and the 10-speed auto to the detriment of the 7-speed manual. Its wide-track HOSS 1.0 suspension combines a lift with 33-inch rubber on beadlock-capable wheels.

Badlands adds Marine Grade Vinyl, and there's also a power-adjustable option on four-door models. The pompously named vinyl upholstery is promoted as being durable and easy to clean. But truth be told, replacing leather with vinyl is a trade-off rather than an upgrade.
